newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares end firm, recover early losses.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares end firm, recover early losses.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended firm in active trade on Tuesday after recovering from an early slide spurred by Wall Street's slip on Monday night, dealers said.
The industrial index added 55.4 points to reach 8,624.2 at close and the all-share index was up 47.3 points at 7,333.6.
The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said the all-share index was at an all time closing high.
The industrial index was also at its highest since January 25, 1996 when it was at 8,739.2 points.

The Dow recorded its second-largest point decline ever on Monday, finishing down 192.25 points to 7,604.26 following comments from Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Japan could sell U.S. Treasuries and switch funds to gold.
But Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Tuesday tried to diffuse the impact of Hashimoto's comments, saying the prime minister had been incorrectly reported.
Golds failed to follow much of the positive trend of the industrials and continued on shaky ground to end steady as the bullion price remained weak, dealers said.
The gold index finished at 3.5 points higher at 1,018.6.
The dealers said also defying gloom was the market's financial sector which continued to roar to new territory on Tuesday as the financial index closed at an all-time high of 10,080.1.
The JSE said the previous high of 9,973 was recorded on Monday, June 23.
Dealers said they expected the market to continue at firmer levels on Wednesday as it awaits the May consumer price index figure due out at 0900 GMT for more direction.
